text:
Jordan: Heads up — after landing the KV int4+FP8 fallback we started seeing tail-latency spikes on canary. Putting notes here.
Maria: Yup, saw that on the perf dash. 99.9th jumped from ~180ms -> ~420ms under mixed small-batch traffic :grimacing:.
Jordan: I could repro locally with the small_char_batch profile. Logs point to slab evictions in the KV allocator right at the spike boundary.
Sam: Can you paste the profiler snippet / logs so we can see where time is going?
Jordan: Sure — short log excerpt:
```
[2026-05-03T02:13:21Z] decode:start id=abc123 batch=6
[2026-05-03T02:13:21Z] kv:lookup pages=24 hits=18 misses=6
[2026-05-03T02:13:21Z] evict_slab: freed 12 pages -> memcpy 2.4ms
[2026-05-03T02:13:21Z] kernel: switch fp8_kv -> int4_decode (thresholds)
[2026-05-03T02:13:21Z] decode:emit token latency=412ms
```
Looks like repeated slab frees + kernel handoffs coincide with the big latency outliers.
Lee: This matches intuition — packing for int4 changes alignment and page usage. When we toggle kernels mid-request we end up doing extra packing/unpacking and unaligned memcpy which thrashes the allocator.
Maria: Also remember we recently lowered the batching threshold to favor faster latency for p95. That increased the proportion of small batches (<=8), which exacerbates KV churn under mixed precision.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout v0.89.3 -> 3/4 healthy (observed lat spikes)
deploy-bot: rolling back to v0.89.2 scheduled on request.
Sam: Quick experiments worth trying:
- force single kernel path (KERNEL_FORCE=fp8_kv) to measure delta
- add allocator padding (KV_PAD=64/128) to reduce fragmentation
- add hysteresis to kernel-switch logic so short bursts don't flip kernels
Jordan: Ran KV_PAD=128 + KERNEL_FORCE unset (so it still can switch). 99.9th dropped from ~420ms -> ~210ms, memory increased ~5%. Baseline p50/p95 stayed ~same. I pushed flamegraphs to the perf bucket (link: https://perf.redwood/internal/kv/17685 — ping me if you need access).
Maria: Good signal. I think we need two parallel fixes: short-term padding + canary rollback rules; medium-term: kernel-switch hysteresis + batch-aware routing.
Lee: I'll open a PR with hysteresis + TTL for kernel choice. We should only allow int4 path when sustained avg batch_size >= 16 for >= 30s. Also add an opt-in knob for allocator padding per-instance type.
Sam: Also we should add a qa/regression that runs the tiny-batch decode with latest calibrations — FYI some int4 calibrations produce more compact encodings which changes page walk patterns and may increase decompression cost.
Jordan: Filed issue #3124 with repro script and attached log traces. I'll run a/b with hysteresis on canary tonight and collect nvprof/flamegraphs.
Maria: Thanks — tagging @oncall for the evening window. If p99 jumps > 2x, auto-rollback.
oncall: Acknowledged, will monitor and abort if we see >300ms p99 sustained for 2min.
Sam: Follow-ups: (1) PR for hysteresis (Lee), (2) add KV_PAD env flag (Lee/Jordan), (3) add a tiny-batch quant calibration regression test (Sam/Maria), (4) canary A/B run tonight (Jordan/@oncall).
Jordan: I'll update the runbook with the experiment steps and the commands I used.
Maria: Great. We'll iterate tomorrow with perf numbers. Thanks everyone :rocket:
